av_event.line_text: Honestly, you'd be surprised. Once you start looking you see them everywhere. I saw a kestrel this morning by the bus stop, just hovering over the verge.
av_event.what: In the lower right corner of Megan's frame, the fleece blanket draped over the guinea pig cage visibly shifts and bulges as the animal moves about underneath it, then settles again.

text:
B: Hiya! Can you hear me alright?
A: Hi! Yeah, yeah I can hear you. Sorry, I've never done one of these before, I'm a bit nervous, I don't know why.
B: Oh don't be, I'm the same. I'm Jade. I'm in Barnsley.
A: I'm Megan, I'm in Chelmsford, so like Essex. Erm, did you do the puzzle bit at the start?
B: Oh my god, the puzzle. I got about halfway and then I were just clicking things, honestly. Did you finish it?
A: Kind of? I ran out of time on the last one. I just kept staring at it, do you know what I mean? Like the shapes stopped looking like shapes.
B: Yeah! That's exactly it.
A: Erm, so what do you do? Sorry, is that, is that alright to ask?
B: No, it's fine. I'm a nail tech. Well, I were. The salon I worked at shut down about eight months ago, so I'm kind of between things at the minute. I'm meant to be setting up doing nails from home. I've bought half the kit for it and it's just sat in the spare room in boxes. Like I've got the lamps and that, I just need to sort insurance and a booking thing and I keep putting it off. Do you know what I mean?
A: Oh, I totally get that. That's like me with my coursework. Are those your nails now? They look really nice.
B: Yeah, did them myself last night. They're like a pinky almond. I were bored.
A: That's so cool. I couldn't do that, I can't even do nail varnish without getting it everywhere.
B: Everyone says that. It's just practice, honestly. What about you, are you at uni?
A: Yeah, second year. Wildlife, Ecology and Conservation Science, which is a bit of a mouthful. Erm, it's out at Writtle, just outside Chelmsford. Basically we do a lot of fieldwork, like bird surveys and pond dipping and trapping li'le mammals, voles and shrews, and then you let them go obviously. That's my favourite bit. The writing up, the stats, I'm not so good at. I kind of panic.
B: Aw, that sounds dead nice though. Is that a bird chart behind you?
A: Yeah! Sorry, it's a bit nerdy. It's just so I can learn them.
B: No it's not, it's cute. I wouldn't know a robin from a pigeon, me.
A: Honestly, you'd be surprised. Once you start looking you see them everywhere. I saw a kestrel this morning by the bus stop, just hovering over the verge.
B: Mm.
A: Have you got any pets? Sorry, random.
B: Yeah, we've got a Staffy, Bella. She's a nightmare. She chewed the remote again on Tuesday and Liam had to order a new one off Amazon. She's lovely though, she just thinks everything's a toy.
A: Aw, I love Staffies. We've got a guinea pig, Biscuit. He's a rescue. He squeaks every time the fridge opens because he thinks it's food.
B: Oh, that's so funny. Bless him.
A: Is Liam your boyfriend?
B: Husband, three years now. He's a sparky. He's working over Wakefield this week, so I've just been sat in with Bella watching Married at First Sight, like a proper sad case.
A: No, that sounds ideal, honestly. My boyfriend does deliveries so he's out all hours. I just read and do sketches and stuff.
B: You draw as well?
A: Erm, a bit. Birds and plants mostly. I don't really show anyone, it's kind of... it's just for me, do you know what I mean?
B: You should though. I bet they're well good. Like, I'm always putting my nails on Instagram and half of them are rubbish.
A: Maybe. Oh, I think we've only got like a minute left.
B: Is it? That's gone dead quick.
A: Sorry, I've been talking about birds the whole time.
B: Don't be daft, I've loved it.
